artifacts.summary: Locates every held-live/held-stale read site, confirms the context-dependent misreading, the stall_suspected zero-commit boundary, task 376's non-widening ruling and prevention-half prior art, the Check H lint precedent, and the reusable session-registry fixture pattern; gives sited recommendations for both the detection and prevention halves.

memory_candidates.content: task-lock.sh check's held-live state (stale heartbeat + session registry pid-alive) is correctly read as 'healthy, do not steal' during lock acquisition, but the SAME exit code (1, shared with held-fresh) is misread as healthy by every other exit-code-only consumer (reconcile-task-status.sh's demote_stranded_status, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's lock PROBE) because they branch on cmd_check's exit code alone and never grep the output line's held-live/held-fresh text prefix the way cmd_acquire's own cross-task overlap pass does. A stall-detection consumer needs the opposite reading of the same state, and must parse the text prefix, not just the exit code.

scripts/test-session-registry.sh constructs a deterministic 'live pid, stale heartbeat' fixture with write_session_fixture "$SESSIONS_DIR" "<id>" "$$" ... <age_minutes> -- using the test script's own PID as a guaranteed-live stand-in and a synthetic age via controlled epoch arithmetic, with no real sleeping. Reuse this pattern verbatim for any future test needing a held-live task-lock state instead of re-deriving a background-process fixture.
